Know what each result establishes.

A local proof, a source argument and an accepted financial transaction are different kinds of evidence.

Current maturity
EXPERIMENTAL · PROPOSED

Moriarty Webs is a concept under review. Supplied records include one current-Rust invoice-partial Groth16 roundtrip (S07) and seven finite local compiled-C2-wrapper cases (S08: one acceptance and six mutation rejections), with a single-party test setup whose operator can forge proofs and caller-fabricated proof contexts. No on-chain transaction is recorded. Only a conditional lowering argument is adopted. V2 consumer descriptions on this page are Opus readings of unadopted, uncompiled source, not observed behavior or exact-source correspondence to those runs. General Web integration, genuine intent authorization, onchain settlement and all-family compatibility remain unestablished in this packet. Local VM cost is not ledger cost. Every interactive example on this page is an illustration.

actions.action: Open Evidence disclosure “What is a Strand?”
actions.observed:
What is a Strand?

An individual proof with its claim, statement and binding metadata. Before a proof exists, say requirement or planned proof. A signed owner intent, UTxO, claim output, validator, catalogue entry, pattern or predicate is not a Strand.
